defect: A second coordinator startup/stop could force-delete every labelled live job on the same Docker daemon. Original method counted attempted deletion as success and trusted raw listing identifiers.
correction: Finite shell-free docker commands, full64hex identifiers, exact xroga-bj names and labels, stopped/nonpaused/nonrestarting/no-restart state, inactive internal networks, no force/volumes flags, count only successful daemon removal.32resource caps per class,10s work deadline,5s command timeout and1MiB output bound.
authority: These operator scripts instantiate trusted server host code, not public request bodies. Cleanup never starts a browser, grants tenant authority, calls a model, reads customer files or creates network access. Existing task finally cleanup remains bound to its own lease-derived names.

verification.negative: Original fake command port reproduced deletion of live and foreign resources. Repaired actual method retains them, refuses malformed IDs/labels, skips attached networks, and counts restart/attach deletion failure as zero.
verification.positive: Exact stopped labelled browser and unused internal job network removed. Existing container protocol, cancellation and sandbox spec tests pass.
verification.executionScope: Actual TypeScript method executed against deterministic injected Docker command port. No live Docker daemon resources mutated. Daemon race guarantees based on official Docker semantics, not a claimed live concurrency experiment.

limitations: Running leftovers are deliberately retained for lease-aware operator review. This method cannot establish an abandoned running job solely from a label.
No live host rollout or broader browser consequential-action authority acceptance.
